Local resistance to continuous perturbations is distinct from stability against formation of a different phase; kinetic persistence can occur without global thermodynamic stability. The selected Gibbs fluid critical endpoint is where two coexisting phases become indistinguishable, and is not a universal criterion for every continuous ordering transition. Finite-system coexistence/interface effects, structural correlations, annealing persistence and simulated molecular reorientation are different observables and inferences, rather than interchangeable phase-boundary measurements.

Static ambient-water pair correlations and SPC/E hydrogen-bond exchange do not by themselves locate a liquid-solid coexistence curve, melting temperature, metastability domain or critical point.

Reported finite-size inference is not direct measurement of an infinite limit. An equilibrium finite-box pressure loop is not automatically a nonequilibrium hysteresis loop, and Monte Carlo displacement time is not a physical nucleation clock.

records.description: In the specified free Maxwell theory, fix an inertial frame, hbar=c=1 and nonzero momentum p. Locally choose a real transverse basis E(p)=(epsilon_1,epsilon_2), with E^T E=I and p^T E=0. For the existing one-photon wavepacket use dPi_p=d^3p/(2pi)^3 and f_r(p)=g(p)c_r(p), where c_dagger c=1 on the nonzero support of g, integral dPi_p |g|^2=1 and integral dPi_p |p| |g|^2 is finite. Its complex polarization vector is e(p)=E(p)c(p), so p dot e=0 and e_dagger e=1. Here e is a polarization amplitude, not the mean electric field, which vanishes in this one-photon number state. A passive real O(p) in SO(2) gives E'=E O, c'=O^T c and f'=O^T f in the transformed mode convention; transforming creation operators consistently preserves e and the one-photon state. An active polarization comparison instead fixes the basis and apparatus while varying relative coefficients. Both transverse modes have the same free frequency |p|; this model supplies no polarization-dependent propagation splitting or preferred vacuum axis.
